alternatives.description: Leave provider/model eligibility to existing reviewer configuration and per-call routing without a durable human exclusion record.
alternatives.projected_effect: No repository change, but the explicit human vendor preference is not represented as a fail-closed Garden operating constraint.
alternatives.risk: Future model-list, aggregator, or fallback edits could unintentionally route Garden work to a vendor the human explicitly excluded.

alternatives.description: Record Anthropic/Claude and NVIDIA/Nemotron as excluded for Garden operational use while preserving historical references and making no misconduct allegation as fact.
alternatives.projected_effect: Creates a durable operator routing constraint that downstream adapters can enforce without changing canonical Garden semantics or authority.
alternatives.risk: Reduced reviewer/provider diversity and possible future provider availability constraints; policy must remain distinguishable from factual claims about the excluded companies.

bidirectional_gaps.gap: No durable, machine-readable expression of the human's explicit provider/model exclusion preference.
Operational flexibility and some model/provider diversity are intentionally reduced until a future explicit human directive changes the policy.

assumptions: The user explicitly directed Garden not to use or actively contact Anthropic or NVIDIA for Garden work.
The user's suspicion about possible misconduct or poisoning is not treated as established evidence and is not encoded as a factual Garden claim.
Historical and prior-art references may remain for audit/provenance without authorizing operational use.
This operating policy does not change canonical v15.5 semantics, human authority, HSA, rights, or canonical promotion rules.
Only an explicit future human directive may change the exclusion list.
reason.uncertainty: Third-party routing ecosystems can change and may not always expose all hosting lineage. Runtime adapters must therefore enforce known model-origin and provider-endpoint exclusions and fail closed where an excluded identity is implicated but unresolved.
counterexamples: An excluded model is selected through a third-party-hosted route.
An allowed model silently falls back to an excluded provider endpoint.
A reviewer roster reintroduces an excluded family after a configuration edit.
A historical citation is mistakenly treated as permission to contact or route Garden work to an excluded vendor.
The policy text is misread as proof of misconduct rather than a human trust/procurement preference.
reason.conclusion: Propose the noncanonical fail-closed provider exclusion as an explicit human operating constraint; preserve factual neutrality about alleged misconduct and require downstream routing adapters to enforce the exclusion without minting authority.

obligations.statement: The policy can be represented as a noncanonical operating constraint without changing canonical Garden semantics or granting new authority.
All runtime provider/model call surfaces enforce the policy.

items.claim_scope: User explicitly requested Anthropic and NVIDIA be excluded from Garden work and active contact.
Machine-readable noncanonical routing constraint with explicit factual-neutrality and override boundaries.
